blocks.prompt: 6 If \(z_1 = 2 + i\), \(z_2 = 3 - 2i\), \(z_3 = 1 + 3i\) then express \(\dfrac{\overline{z_1}\,\overline{z_3}}{z_2}\) in the form of \(a + ib\).
blocks.explanation: The book prints a conjugate bar over \(z_1\) and over \(z_3\). Plan: write the two conjugates, multiply them, divide by \(z_2\) using the conjugate of \(z_2\), and split into \(a + ib\). (Even if one bar covered the whole product, the answer is the same, because \(\overline{z_1 z_3} = \overline{z_1}\,\overline{z_3}\).)
steps:
Step 1: Write the conjugates
\[\overline{z_1} = 2 - i\]
\[\overline{z_3} = 1 - 3i\]
Why: Keep the real part, change the sign of the imaginary part.

Step 2: Multiply the conjugates
\[(2 - i)(1 - 3i)\]
\[= 2 - 6i - i + 3i^{2}\]
\[= 2 - 7i - 3\]
\[= -1 - 7i\]
Why: Each term times each term; \((-i)(-3i) = 3i^2 = -3\).

Step 3: Multiply by the conjugate of \(z_2\)
\[\dfrac{-1 - 7i}{3 - 2i} \cdot \dfrac{3 + 2i}{3 + 2i}\]
Why: \(\overline{z_2} = 3 + 2i\) makes the bottom real.

Step 5: Work out the bottom
\[(3 - 2i)(3 + 2i) = 9 - 4i^{2}\]
\[= 9 + 4 = 13\]
Why: Difference of squares.

Step 6: Write as \(a + ib\)
\[\dfrac{11 - 23i}{13} = \dfrac{11}{13} - \dfrac{23}{13}i\]
Why: Divide each part by 13.
